## Purpose

This procedure describes the operation, maintenance, and troubleshooting
of the Bio-Rad QX200 Droplet Digital PCR (ddPCR) system, including the
QX200 Droplet Generator, the C1000 Touch Thermal Cycler with the 96-well
Deep Well Reaction Module, and the QX200 Droplet Reader. The QX200
partitions each PCR reaction into approximately 20,000 nanoliter-sized
droplets, enabling absolute quantification of target DNA sequences
without a standard curve. For assay design, primer/probe sequences, and
data analysis, see
[SOP-L701 ddPCR Nitrogen Cycle Primers](SOP-L701-ddpcr-nitrogen-cycle-primers.qmd)
and
[SOP-L702 ddPCR Data Analysis](SOP-L702-ddpcr-data-analysis.qmd).


## Scope

- **Applies to:** All use of the Bio-Rad QX200 ddPCR system in the EA
  Program laboratory, including droplet generation, thermal cycling,
  and droplet reading
- **Does not apply to:** Assay design, primer validation, or data
  analysis (see SOP-L701 and SOP-L702); conventional qPCR on other
  instruments
- **Location:** *TBD* (confirm room and bench assignment)

## Definitions

- **Amplitude:** The fluorescence signal intensity of a droplet; positive droplets (containing target DNA) have high amplitude; negative droplets have low amplitude; a clear separation between positive and negative populations is required for accurate quantification.
- **Droplet digital PCR (ddPCR):** A method of absolute quantification of nucleic acids in which the sample is partitioned into ~20,000 nanoliter-sized water-in-oil droplets, each containing zero or one target molecule; after PCR amplification, the fraction of fluorescent positive droplets is used to calculate target concentration using Poisson statistics.
- **FAM:** A green fluorescent dye (fluorescein amidite) used to label one probe or primer in a duplex ddPCR assay; detected in the FAM channel (channel 1) by the QX200.
- **HEX:** A yellow-orange fluorescent dye used to label a second probe in a duplex ddPCR assay, or as an alternative to VIC; detected in channel 2 by the QX200.
- **Poisson correction:** A statistical adjustment applied by the DropletQuant software to account for the probability that some droplets contain more than one target molecule; necessary when target concentrations are high.
- **Copies per microliter (copies/µL):** The absolute concentration of the target DNA in the final ddPCR reaction, as reported by DropletQuant; must be back-calculated to the original sample concentration using the appropriate dilution factor.
- **Threshold:** The fluorescence amplitude boundary separating positive from negative droplets; set manually or automatically in the analysis software; incorrect threshold setting is the most common source of ddPCR quantification error.

## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Chemical:** Droplet generation oil (Bio-Rad Cat. 1863005) is a
  fluorinated oil. Avoid skin contact and inhalation. Work in a
  well-ventilated area or fume hood when handling bulk oil. Review the
  SDS before first use.
- **Biological:** Samples may contain environmental DNA from unknown
  organisms. Treat all samples and amplified products as potentially
  biohazardous.
- **Physical:** The thermal cycler reaches temperatures up to 98 C.
  Allow the block to cool before removing plates. The Droplet Reader
  needle is sharp; do not reach into the reader bay.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Safety glasses
- [ ] Lab coat
- [ ] Nitrile gloves (change between pre-PCR and post-PCR areas)

### Emergency Procedures

For oil spills, absorb with paper towels and dispose as chemical waste.
For thermal burns, apply cool running water and seek first aid. Refer to
[SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd) and
[SOP-L003 Hazardous Materials Handling](SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd).

## Procedure

### Pre-PCR Setup (Clean Area)

::: {.callout-important}
All pre-PCR work (reaction assembly, droplet generation) must be
performed in the designated pre-PCR area to prevent amplicon
contamination. Use dedicated pipettes and wear clean gloves.
:::

1. Thaw the ddPCR Supermix and DNA templates on ice
2. Prepare the reaction master mix according to the assay protocol
   (see SOP-L701 for primer/probe concentrations and cycling conditions)
3. Dispense 20 uL of each assembled reaction into the sample wells
   (middle row) of a DG8 cartridge
4. Add 70 uL of Droplet Generation Oil to the oil wells (bottom row)
5. Attach a DG8 gasket to the cartridge

### Droplet Generation

1. Place the loaded cartridge into the QX200 Droplet Generator
2. Close the lid and press **Start**. Generation takes approximately
   2 minutes per cartridge.
3. When complete, carefully open the lid. Do not tilt or shake the
   cartridge -- the droplets are fragile.
4. Using a multichannel pipette set to 40 uL, gently aspirate the
   droplets from the top row of the cartridge and dispense into the
   96-well plate. Pipette slowly (approximately 3 seconds to aspirate,
   3 seconds to dispense) to avoid shearing droplets.
5. Repeat for each cartridge

### Plate Sealing

1. Place the pierceable foil heat seal over the loaded 96-well plate
2. Seal using the PX1 PCR Plate Sealer at 180 C for 5 seconds
3. Visually confirm a uniform seal across all wells

### Thermal Cycling

1. Place the sealed plate into the C1000 Touch Thermal Cycler with the
   96-Deep Well Reaction Module
2. Program the thermal cycling protocol per SOP-L701 (typical: 95 C
   activation, 40 cycles of denaturation/annealing, 98 C droplet
   stabilization, 4 C hold)
3. Set the ramp rate to 2 C/s (critical for ddPCR; do not use the
   default maximum ramp rate)
4. Start the run. Cycling typically takes 2--2.5 hours.
5. After cycling, plates can be held at 4 C for up to 24 hours before
   reading, but immediate reading is preferred

### Droplet Reading

1. Open QuantaSoft software on the connected computer
2. Set up the plate layout: assign sample names, target names,
   experiment type (ABS for absolute quantification), and supermix type
3. Place the sealed plate into the QX200 Droplet Reader
4. Confirm that the reader waste and buffer bottles are at appropriate
   levels (refill or empty as needed before starting a full plate)
5. Tap **Start** to begin reading. The reader processes each well
   individually (approximately 1--2 minutes per well).
6. Monitor the first few wells to confirm that droplet counts exceed
   10,000 accepted events per well

### Data Review

1. After reading, review the 1-D amplitude plots in QuantaSoft to
   verify clear separation between positive and negative droplet
   clusters
2. Set the fluorescence amplitude threshold manually using the NTC
   and positive control wells as guides
3. Check that all wells have at least 10,000 accepted droplets; flag
   any wells below this threshold
4. Export results as .csv for downstream analysis (see SOP-L702)

### Shutdown and Daily Maintenance

1. Remove the plate from the Droplet Reader
2. Check the reader waste bottle; empty if more than 75% full
3. Check the reader buffer bottle; refill if less than 25% full
4. Wipe down the Droplet Generator cartridge holder with a lint-free
   tissue
5. Dispose of used cartridges and gaskets (see Section 8)
6. Close QuantaSoft and shut down instruments if no further runs are
   scheduled


## Quality Control and Acceptance Criteria

- Every run must include: no-template controls (NTC, minimum 2 wells),
  extraction blanks (from SOP-L700), and positive controls (gBlock or
  plasmid at known concentration)
- Droplet count per well must exceed 10,000 accepted droplets (out of
  approximately 20,000 generated); wells below this threshold should be
  excluded
- NTC wells must show 0 or fewer than 3 positive droplets; more than 3
  indicates contamination and the plate or affected target should be
  rerun
- Positive/negative droplet cluster separation must be unambiguous on
  the 1-D amplitude plot
- *TBD -- define acceptable coefficients of variation for technical
  replicates (typically less than 15--25% for ddPCR)*
- *TBD -- establish a maintenance log and schedule for Bio-Rad service
  visits*

## Training Record

Before using the QX200 system independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP, [SOP-L701](SOP-L701-ddpcr-nitrogen-cycle-primers.qmd),
   and [SOP-L003 Hazardous Materials Handling](SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd)
2. Complete the Bio-Rad QX200 online training modules or equivalent
   manufacturer training
3. Observe a trained operator demonstrate droplet generation, thermal
   cycling setup, and droplet reading for a full plate
4. Perform a supervised run including reaction assembly, droplet
   generation, plate sealing, thermal cycling, and reading
5. Demonstrate competence in QuantaSoft plate setup and threshold
   setting
6. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager


## Appendix A: Troubleshooting {.appendix}

| Symptom                              | Probable Cause                     | Corrective Action                          |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------|
| Low droplet count (below 10,000)      | Pipetting error during transfer; clogged cartridge | Pipette more slowly (3 s up, 3 s down); use a fresh cartridge |
| No separation between positive and negative clusters | Poor primer/probe design; degraded reagents | Review assay (SOP-L701); use fresh Supermix |
| Rain (droplets between clusters)      | Suboptimal annealing temperature; partial inhibition | Run a temperature gradient; dilute template |
| Reader error or blockage              | Air bubble or debris in reader line | Run a cleaning cycle per Bio-Rad instructions; contact lab manager |
| Positive droplets in NTC wells        | Amplicon contamination             | Decontaminate pre-PCR area with 10% bleach; use fresh reagents; separate pre- and post-PCR areas strictly |
